title: Geometric factorization through stratified pro-etale charts
statement: Let f:X→Y be a separated, locally finite type, quasi-compact morphism of schemes and let C(T,g) be an arbitrary property of a scheme T equipped with a map g:T→Y. Suppose that every affine open V of Y admits a finite qcqs open-closed tree [def-sfb-qcqs-open-closed-tree] such that each nonempty leaf has a finite jointly surjective family of qcqs pro-etale charts A_i with C(A_i,A_i→V→Y). Then every affine open U of X admits such a tree and such finite qcqs pro-etale chart covers, and every resulting chart B has a factorization B→T→Y of B→U→X→Y with C(T,T→Y). No preservation of C under pullback is required and no condition is imposed on empty leaves.

source.place: Tag 09C3 local-structure argument; Tag 09Y4 finite constructible stratification and Tags 09YD, 09YG constructible images. Agent-written finite chart-factorization assembly.

proof.text: For each point of affine U choose an affine neighborhood V of its image and an affine neighborhood B contained in its inverse image. Compactness gives a finite such cover B_j of U and maps g_j:B_j→V_j with g_j V_j.ι=B_j.ι U.ι f. Choose the supplied source tree on each V_j. Enumerate its leaves recursively by a finite sum type: a leaf contributes a singleton and a split contributes the sum of its child indices. Induction proves that the leaf maps are quasi-compact immersions, their domains are qcqs, their images are constructible, and those images cover the root. Constructibility at an open edge follows from quasi-compactness of the open immersion; at a closed edge its complement is the range of the quasi-compact open child.

For every j and source leaf L, form D=B_j×_{V_j}L and its immersion d:D→B_j→U. Its image is the image under B_j→U of the inverse image under g_j of the constructible leaf image; hence it is constructible. The ranges of all these finitely many d cover U by the pullback range formula. Reuse the geometric partition_tree construction from AffineResidueLisseTree locally to avoid its expensive arithmetic import. Apply exists_constructible_cut to each immersion S→U, factoring it as a closed immersion into a quasi-compact open O whose complement of S is also quasi-compact. Pull back the split into O and its closed complement, and then within O the split into O minus S and S. A leaf either avoids S or factors through S. Induction over the finite immersion indices using SchemeRefinementTree.bind preserves all previously resolved ranges, and coverage forces every nonempty final leaf to factor through a member of the family. Forgetting the structural maps gives a finite qcqs open-closed tree over U and a map from every nonempty output leaf S to one of the D commuting over U.

Compose S→D with D→L. Since S is nonempty, so is L, and the assumed finite source pro-etale chart family A_i→L is available. Define the output chart as S×_L A_i→S. It is pro-etale by base change; its domain is qcqs since A_i and S are qcqs and any morphism from a quasi-compact scheme to the quasi-separated L is quasi-compact. The pullback range formula shows that this family covers S. Its second projection to A_i, the source map A_i→L→V_j→Y and the two fibre-product equations give the required factorization; C is retained on the original A_i, rather than transported.

proof_origin.place: Agent-written finite-cover assembly from Tag 09Y4, with source charts from Tag 09C3; proof reuses the existing proved partition_tree construction locally, using only its geometric dependencies.

mathlib_searches.query: Refine a finite cover by constructible locally closed subschemes to a finite open closed tree whose leaves factor through the covering subschemes
mathlib_searches.results: Eight general finiteSubcover and affineRefinement hits; no finite open-closed chart-factorization theorem. Local library search found the proved private partition_tree construction.
One hit supplies constructible inverse images of scheme morphisms. Together with pullback range and constructible image lemmas it supplies the geometric inputs, not the full tree or chart assembly.

Twenty-five topology hits include the constructible-image lemmas and finite neighborhood subcover. No chart-factorization theorem. Blueprint searches for open closed tree and 09Y4 both returned zero nodes.

from.place: Finite-projective local model transport, geometric refinement and chart factorization before algebraic pullback.

lean.statement:
theorem affineOpenClosedChartFactorization
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (_hs : IsSeparated f) (_ht : LocallyOfFiniteType f) (_hq : QuasiCompact f)
    (C : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}), (T ⟶ Y) → Prop)
    (hC : ∀ (V : Y.Opens), IsAffine V.toScheme →
      ∃ tree : QcqsOpenClosedTree V.toScheme,
        ∀ (S : Scheme.{u}) (p : tree.Path S), p.IsLeaf → Nonempty S →
          ∃ (c : ℕ) (A : Fin c → S.ProEt),
            (∀ i, CompactSpace (A i).left) ∧
            (∀ i, QuasiSeparatedSpace (A i).left) ∧
            (∀ x : S, ∃ i, x ∈ Set.range (A i).hom.base) ∧
            ∀ i, C (A i).left ((A i).hom ≫ p.toRoot ≫ V.ι))
    (U : X.Opens) [IsAffine U.toScheme] :
    ∃ tree : QcqsOpenClosedTree U.toScheme,
      ∀ (S : Scheme.{u}) (p : tree.Path S), p.IsLeaf → Nonempty S →
        ∃ (c : ℕ) (A : Fin c → S.ProEt),
          (∀ i, CompactSpace (A i).left) ∧
          (∀ i, QuasiSeparatedSpace (A i).left) ∧
          (∀ x : S, ∃ i, x ∈ Set.range (A i).hom.base) ∧
          ∀ i, ∃ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : T ⟶ Y) (h : (A i).left ⟶ T),
            C T g ∧ ((A i).hom ≫ p.toRoot ≫ U.ι) ≫ f = h ≫ g
